Well I happen to know because I took this footage!

This was taken at the "afterglow" party during the 2013 Sutter Creek Ragtime Festival.

I posted this partly because the 2015 festival is this weekend, and I'm really stoked about it (I'm going to be performing as well).

This house is known as "Skunk Hollow" and is kind of like a Victorian-esque mansion in the middle Sutter Creek. Many of the performers stay at this private residence during the festival, and obviously numerous instruments are available for the occasion!

Here are some some highlights from the last few years of the festival:

Carl Sonny Leyland plays the best boogie woogie I've ever seen

Tom Brier and Virginia Tichenor play Swipesy Cakewalk by Arthur Marshall and Scott Joplin

Frederick Hodges plays "Broadway Melody" by Nacio Herb Brown and Arthur Freed

Squeek Steele and Gary Greenlund at the 2013 Sutter Creek Ragtime Festival

Patrick Aranda plays Ida, Sweet as Apple Cider at the 2013 Sutter Creek Ragtime Festival

Flurries by Frank LiVolsi - Tom Brier & I (piano) - Julia Riley (flute) - Kitty Wilson (washboard)

TLDR; "Technology is hard to predict. Social Security is bad because it doesn't evolve quickly in a free market model."

I don't agree that the free market can make everything better and cheaper, particularly when people's lives are on the line. We are willing to pay extra for an unreasonable degree of security, and it doesn't have anything to do with free market ideals. For example, it would make perfect economic sense to cut off expensive medical care if the patient has already passed their average life expectancy... It's just not a good investment. I completely disagree, and the only way people will buy into the system is if there's a guarantee of safety.
